s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive purpura and ecchymoses with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura
Amorphous eosinophilic deposits on hematoxylin-eosin staining
Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura and ecchymoses
Periorbital involvement initially
Progression of purpura and ecchymoses over 12 months
Anorexia and weight loss
Alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment in medical history
Elder abuse excluded
Anemia, abnormal liver function, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis
Unremarkable radiological studies
4-mm punch biopsy showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits

shortlist.label: Primary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive purpura and ecchymoses with systemic symptoms, along with biopsy findings of upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits and positive Congo red staining

shortlist.label: Senile systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's age and clinical presentation of purpura and ecchymoses, which are common in senile systemic amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of anemia, abnormal liver function, and renal impairment, which can be associated with light-chain amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura in the periocular, neck, axillary, trunk, and inguinal regions, consistent with cutaneous amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Dysproteinemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Normal serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis, but clinical presentation suggestive of dysproteinemic amyloidosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, weight loss, and systemic involvement such as anemia, abnormal liver function, and renal impairment, along with the biopsy findings of amorphous eosinophilic deposits that stained positive with Congo red and demonstrated apple-green birefringence under polarized light, is most consistent with primary systemic amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Senile systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents later in life with less systemic involvement and does not usually cause purpura or ecchymoses

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: Would likely have abnormal serum protein electrophoresis or immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis results, which were normal in this case

rejected.label: Cutaneous amyloidosis
rejected.why: Primarily involves the skin without systemic manifestations, which does not fit the patient's multi-systemic symptoms

rejected.label: Dysproteinemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: Refers to amyloidosis associated with plasma cell dyscrasias, which would also likely have abnormal serum protein electrophoresis or immunofixation results
